clue.text: Jacob, for example, is hot with embarrassment

parts.note: the Jacob is a piebald breed of sheep, so it is an example of that animal
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone called Jacob flushes red with embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob looks like a man's name, but here it is the Jacob sheep breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sheepish looks abashed and awkward, the manner of a person feeling embarrassment.

clue.text: Trivial discourtesy?

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning minor or negligible, as in a small injury
a noun meaning a snub or insult

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means small and unimportant; as a noun it means an insulting snub.

clue.text: Hire me to turn up with device

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word me is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a device can be a ploy, a cunning scheme or trick

explanation.surface: Someone offers to be taken on along with a gadget of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' turns ME into EM in this down clue; 'with' joins it to PLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a worker is to engage them for pay, a synonym of hire.

clue.text: Bird pecking university student's garment

indicators.note: a bird pecking at something has its beak in it, so the bird's letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: the plover is a wading bird
L, for learner, stands for a student, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A bird pecks at the clothing of a university student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pecking' sets U and L (learner, a student) inside PLOVER, after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a knitted jumper put on over the head, a type of clothing.

clue.text: Flag, in the kitchen?

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to weaken or droop, as energy flags
the basin in a kitchen where dishes are washed

explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to decline or drop, as spirits do; the kitchen fixture is the basin with taps for washing up.

clue.text: Central European currency that's popular? Keep out!

indicators.note: Keep goes on the outside, so the word for popular sits within the keep's letters

parts.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort
IN means popular or fashionable, as in 'the in crowd'

explanation.surface: A warning that a popular foreign currency is off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep out!' reads like a sign; here 'out' tells you FORT goes outside IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is the monetary unit of Hungary, a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Nothing sour, at first sniff, for the nose to detect

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
dour means sour or sullen in manner

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word sniff is wanted

explanation.surface: At the first sniff, nothing smells off to the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Smells are what a nose picks up, so they are things for it to detect.

clue.text: Gate-crashers' red van is overturned

definitions.note: the definition is the plural noun, with the apostrophe only part of the surface

indicators.note: an overturned vehicle ends up in a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A red van belonging to party gate-crashers has been tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' suggests a reversal, but REDVANIS backwards gives nothing; it is an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaders enter where they are not welcome, as uninvited intruders at a party do.

clue.text: Insisted constituents produce sense of order

indicators.note: the constituents, or component letters, of the word are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A demand that a sense of order be imposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is neatness, the state of everything being arranged properly in its place.

clue.text: Spitting, and I appear to be turning ashen

parts.note: the letter I as written
the verb am, as in 'I am', contracted to just M in 'I'm'
paling means going pale, turning the colour of ash

explanation.surface: A frightened person spits and goes grey in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I appear to be turning ashen' as 'I'm paling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaling means skewering, as meat is run through on a spit for roasting.

clue.text: Crow — divorce reform out east!

indicators.note: to reform is to form anew, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letter for east is taken out of the word divorce

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A crow squawking a call for divorce law reform in the eastern region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from DIVORCE, and 'reform' rearranges what is left, DIVORC.
explanation.definitionFit: Corvid is the family name for crows and their relatives such as rooks, ravens and jays.

clue.text: New version of Lear upset one of Hamlet's cast

indicators.note: a new version reworks the play's title, so its letters are rearranged
in a down clue, up means the word set is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A fresh production of King Lear goes wrong, disturbing a member of the Hamlet company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it splits in two: 'up' tells you to read the following word upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is Polonius's son and Ophelia's brother, a character in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Two rings initially each bird required

parts.note: a hoop is a ring, the first of the two
the letter O, shaped like a ring, is the second

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word each is taken

explanation.surface: Each bird must have two rings, a sort of bird-ringing instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The two rings are different pieces: HOOP and the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested pinkish bird with black and white wings.

clue.text: Battle-axe one man used against another, reportedly

indicators.note: means what follows is how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: two men's names set side by side: Harry next to Dan

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman wielded one man as a weapon against another, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle-axe' looks like a weapon to go with 'used against'; it is an informal word for a domineering older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are insulting terms for a bossy, belligerent old woman.

clue.text: In this way, travelling around unaccompanied is nonsense!

indicators.note: the word for the method of travel goes around the outside of the other piece

parts.note: by, as in 'by this means', says how something is done
alone means without company

explanation.surface: A remark that wandering about with nobody else is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: BY is the word you travel by (by train), so it fits 'In this way, travelling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloney is informal American slang for rubbish or foolish talk.

clue.text: Forms new partnership and makes good

explanation.definitionFit: Read in two parts, the word means coupling up once more; as one word it means fixing or mending.

clue.text: Circus boy with painful back

indicators.note: means the word for painful is read backwards

parts.note: sore means painful or aching

explanation.surface: A circus lad has a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue in Piccadilly Circus, London, is popularly called Eros, the boy god of love; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged archer statue in London's Piccadilly Circus is known as the god of love, depicted as a boy.

clue.text: Repartee of second bird

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back or support it
the chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat

explanation.surface: A question about the witty talk of a second bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is the verb meaning support, not an ordinal.
explanation.definitionFit: Backchat is cheeky answering back, a form of quick-witted retort.

clue.text: Such birds peregrinate to get a lettuce

parts.note: to peregrinate is to travel about, to tour
cos is a long-leaved lettuce variety, also called romaine

explanation.surface: Birds of a certain kind travel far to find a lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peregrinate' hints at the peregrine falcon, but it is the verb meaning travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Turacos are colourful fruit-eating African birds; 'such' points to the plural species.

clue.text: Tearabout constantly showing respect?

indicators.note: the word for tear goes about, or around, the word for constantly

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip in fabric
ever means always or constantly

explanation.surface: A tearaway who shows respect all the time, which seems unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tearabout' reads like a tearaway, the reckless youth; split it into 'Tear' and 'about', the second being the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means deeply respectful, as in reverent silence in church.

clue.text: Soon, Japanese drama will feature in article

indicators.note: the drama will appear within the article, so its letters go inside

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
No, also spelt Noh, is classical Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: Before long, a Japanese play will appear in a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is the grammar term, giving AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly, in a little while.

clue.text: He breaks hearts, but is consistent

indicators.note: he breaks into the other word, so his letters go inside it

parts.note: cores are the hearts or centres of things
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heartbreaker who is nevertheless reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' is the container signal, as in breaking into something; 'but' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together logically, as a consistent argument does.

clue.text: Itch horribly on donning old woollen tunic

indicators.note: an itch that behaves horribly is jumbled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone itches horribly on putting on a scratchy old woollen garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges ITCH to CHIT; 'donning' is a link adding ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiton was a garment worn in ancient Greece, a simple draped tunic of wool or linen.

clue.text: If needing a lift over specific area, transport's provided

definitions.note: the definition is the noun; the 's stands for 'is', linking to 'provided'

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, or above, the second
in a down clue, a lift raises the word if so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an acre is a fixed unit of area

explanation.surface: Advice that if you need a lift over a certain area, vehicles are on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing a lift' turns IF upwards to FI in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiacre is a small horse-drawn hackney carriage, a means of getting about in old Paris.

clue.text: Clothing that fits a cow?

definitions.meaning: a breed of dairy cattle from the Channel Island of the same name

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a knitted pullover and a breed of dairy cattle from a Channel Island, hence the garment fits the beast.

clue.text: Rich keef well wrapped up in it?

definitions.text: Rich keef well wrapped up in it?

indicators.note: something well wrapped up is folded over and round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wraps their potent cannabis neatly in a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Keef, or kif, is cannabis; the whole clue suggests a cloth it could be bundled in.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerchief is a square of cloth, the sort of wrapping a stash could be tied up in.

clue.text: Foul pass

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to pollute or make dirty
a noun meaning a narrow gorge or valley

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pollute or desecrate; as a noun it is a narrow gorge troops must file through.

clue.text: Stock speed trial

definitions.meaning: lineage or breed, as in 'of good stock'
a contest to see who is fastest

explanation.definitionFit: Stock means ancestry or ethnic group; a speed trial is a contest of who is fastest.

clue.text: Goddess Tom first encountered

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so a he-cat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word encountered is taken

explanation.surface: A goddess that a man called Tom met first.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a man's name; it is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, crossroads and the underworld.

clue.text: Converted, dances around church to rhythmic beats

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for church
converted means changed into another form, so the letters of dances are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Converts dance around a church to a steady beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' rearranges the dancers' word, and 'around' wraps the result about the church, which goes in just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is a rise and fall in rhythm, the measured beat of speech, music or marching.

clue.text: Sober, after knocking it back

indicators.note: the word for sober comes after the next piece
means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: sane means sensible and sober

explanation.surface: Someone is sober again after drinking it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking it back' suggests downing a drink, fitting the herbal tea; only 'back' does the turning, and 'after' places the word for sober second.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal tea, the sort of soothing drink one knocks back to stay sober.

clue.text: Hide, when it gets tough!

parts.note: skin that toughens takes on the quality of tanned animal skin, so the adjective describes hide that has hardened

explanation.definitionFit: Something tough and hard like tanned skin is described as like cured hide.
